name.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省横加公路 1 号

tagline.en: Mile 0 at Victoria, and the pass where the country was declared joined
tagline.zh: 零英里碑立于维多利亚，全国贯通的宣告则在罗杰斯山口

start.en: Douglas Street at Dallas Road, on the south-west corner of Beacon Hill Park in Victoria, where the Mile 0 monument stands
start.zh: 维多利亚市灯塔山公园西南角、道格拉斯街与达拉斯路交口，零英里纪念碑所在处

end.en: The Alberta boundary at Kicking Horse Pass, 1,627 m above sea level between Yoho and Banff national parks
end.zh: 踢马山口的艾伯塔省界，海拔 1,627 米，位于幽鹤与班夫两座国家公园之间

en: British Columbia's Highway 1 is the western end of the Trans-Canada, and it is two roads with a boat between them. The first begins at a stone marker in Victoria and runs up Vancouver Island to Nanaimo. The second begins at Horseshoe Bay in West Vancouver and does not stop until the Rockies. Between them is a ninety-five minute sailing across the Strait of Georgia, which BC Ferries describes in its service contract as the main connector for the Trans-Canada highway.

The mainland half is the most demanding stretch of the whole route. It climbs out of the Fraser delta, threads the Fraser Canyon, crosses the dry interior at Kamloops, and then takes three mountain ranges in succession — the Monashees, the Selkirks at Rogers Pass, and the Rockies at Kicking Horse. Rogers Pass is the reason the highway exists in its modern form, and it is where the country was told the road was finished.

The ferry is not drawn on this map and not counted in the distance below. Statistics Canada files ferry connections as a separate class of feature from road segments, and the national road file that this atlas is built from contains only the roads.
zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省的 1 号公路是横加公路的西端，实际上是两条路，中间隔着一艘船。第一段自维多利亚的一座石碑起，沿温哥华岛北上至纳奈莫。第二段自西温哥华的马蹄湾起，一路不停，直抵落基山。两段之间是横渡乔治亚海峡的九十五分钟航程——BC 渡轮在其服务合同中称这条航线为「横加公路的主要连接线」。
大陆一侧是全线最艰难的路段。它自弗雷泽三角洲爬升，穿过弗雷泽峡谷，经坎卢普斯横越干燥的内陆，随后连翻三道山脉：莫纳希山、罗杰斯山口所在的塞尔扣克山，以及踢马山口所在的落基山。罗杰斯山口正是这条公路得以成为今日模样的缘由，也是当年向全国宣告「路修通了」的地方。
渡轮既不在本图上绘出，也不计入下方的里程。加拿大统计局把渡轮连接线归为与路段不同的要素类别，而本图谱所依据的国家道路数据只包含道路。

en: British Columbia signed its agreement under the Trans-Canada Highway Act on 25 April 1950, with six other provinces on the same day. The federal government paid up to half the cost of new construction, and the whole cost of the sections inside national parks — a division that still holds, and which is why Ottawa, not Victoria, maintains the highway through Glacier and Yoho today.

The obstacle was the Selkirk Range. Until 1962 traffic took the Big Bend Highway, a gravel detour that followed the Columbia River two hundred miles around the mountains. Its replacement was a new 45-kilometre road over Rogers Pass through Glacier National Park, and closing that gap was what made it possible to drive across Canada without leaving the country.

It was opened twice, a month apart, for reasons that had nothing to do with engineering. On 30 July 1962 Premier W.A.C. Bennett held British Columbia's own ceremony, calling the road British Columbia Highway No. 1 and not mentioning Canada. On 3 September Prime Minister John Diefenbaker declared the Trans-Canada Highway officially open at Rogers Pass, with representatives of all ten provinces present and the premiers of British Columbia, New Brunswick and Newfoundland absent. Construction under the Act continued for another nine years.
zh: 1950 年 4 月 25 日，不列颠哥伦比亚与另外六省同日签署《横加公路法》下的协议。联邦政府承担新建工程至多一半的费用，国家公园路段则全额承担——这一分工沿用至今，也正因如此，今天穿越冰川与幽鹤两座国家公园的路段由渥太华而非维多利亚养护。
障碍在塞尔扣克山。1962 年以前，车流要走大弯公路——一条沿哥伦比亚河绕行两百英里的碎石便道。取代它的，是穿越冰川国家公园、翻越罗杰斯山口的 45 公里新路；正是这一缺口的闭合，才使人们得以不出国门横穿加拿大。
它开通了两次，相隔一个月，原因与工程毫无关系。1962 年 7 月 30 日，省长 W.A.C. 贝内特举行了不列颠哥伦比亚自己的仪式，称这条路为「不列颠哥伦比亚 1 号公路」，通篇不提加拿大。9 月 3 日，总理约翰·迪芬贝克在罗杰斯山口宣布横加公路正式通车，十省代表到场，而不列颠哥伦比亚、新不伦瑞克与纽芬兰三省省长缺席。法案之下的建设，此后又持续了九年。

en: Rogers Pass receives an average of 8.5 metres of snow a season, and took 16.7 metres in the winter of 1953–54. A road kept open through that had to be defended rather than merely plowed, and the defences were designed before the road was built: the Department of Public Works created an Avalanche Research Group in 1953, whose work cut the length of snow sheds thought necessary from an estimated 1,525 metres to 825 metres.

The remaining defence is artillery. Parks Canada and the Canadian Armed Forces have operated permanent howitzer emplacements at the pass for more than fifty years, firing onto the slopes above the highway to bring down snow deliberately when the road is closed rather than accidentally when it is not. It is the longest-running mobile avalanche control programme in the world.
The pass was designated a national historic site in 1971. The construction of the Trans-Canada Highway as a whole was designated a national historic event in 2014.
zh: 罗杰斯山口每季平均降雪 8.5 米，1953 至 1954 年冬季更达 16.7 米。要在这种条件下保通，靠的不是清雪而是设防，而防护工程在筑路之前就已设计：公共工程部于 1953 年成立雪崩研究组，其成果把原本估算需要的 1,525 米防雪棚缩短到 825 米。
其余的防护手段是火炮。五十多年来，加拿大公园管理局与加拿大武装部队在山口设有固定榴弹炮阵地，向公路上方的坡面射击，在封路时主动把积雪打下来，而不是等它在通车时自己落下。这是世界上运行时间最长的机动雪崩控制计划。
该山口于 1971 年被列为国家历史遗址。横加公路的建设本身，则于 2014 年被定为国家历史事件。

label.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省境内长度

value.en: 552 miles (888 km) of the main route, as published while the road was being finished. No federal department publishes a current provincial figure.
value.zh: 主线 552 英里（888 公里），为工程收尾期间公布的数字。目前没有联邦部门发布现行的分省里程。

figures.source: Canada Year Book 1967, p. 805, Dominion Bureau of Statistics

value.en: 27 miles (45 km) of new road through Glacier National Park, replacing the gravel Big Bend Highway
value.zh: 穿越冰川国家公园的 45 公里新建道路，取代碎石路面的大弯公路

figures.source: MacLeod, “The Trans-Canada Highway — A Major Link in Canada's Transportation System”, Transportation Association of Canada, 2014

value.en: 32 nautical miles from Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay, 1 hour 35 minutes; BC Ferries Route 2, described in the Coastal Ferry Services Contract as the main connector for the Trans-Canada Highway
value.zh: 自马蹄湾至离港湾 32 海里，航时 1 小时 35 分；BC 渡轮 2 号航线，《沿海渡轮服务合同》称其为横加公路的主要连接线

figures.source: BC Ferries, Coastal Ferry Services Contract, Route 2

value.en: 8.5 m in an average season; 16.7 m in 1953–54

label.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省境内造价

why.en: No public figure. The federal total under the Act was $825 million to the provinces plus $76.6 million inside national parks, but the per-province breakdown exists only in the Department of Public Works' 1971 final report, which has not been digitised.
why.zh: 无公开数据。法案之下的联邦支出总额为拨付各省 8.25 亿加元、国家公园路段另加 7,660 万加元，但分省明细仅见于公共工程部 1971 年的最终报告，该报告未数字化。

timeline.en: British Columbia signs its Trans-Canada Highway agreement with Ottawa on 25 April, one of six provinces to sign that day.
timeline.zh: 4 月 25 日，不列颠哥伦比亚与渥太华签署横加公路协议，为当天签署的六省之一。

timeline.en: The Department of Public Works forms an Avalanche Research Group to work out how to keep a road open over Rogers Pass.
timeline.zh: 公共工程部成立雪崩研究组，研究如何让翻越罗杰斯山口的公路保持通行。

timeline.en: The Canadian Automobile Association installs the Mile 0 monument at Beacon Hill Park in Victoria — four years before the highway opens.
timeline.zh: 加拿大汽车协会在维多利亚灯塔山公园立起零英里纪念碑，比公路通车早了四年。

timeline.en: Premier W.A.C. Bennett opens the Rogers Pass road for British Columbia on 30 July; Prime Minister Diefenbaker declares the Trans-Canada Highway open at the pass on 3 September.
timeline.zh: 7 月 30 日，省长 W.A.C. 贝内特代表不列颠哥伦比亚为罗杰斯山口公路剪彩；9 月 3 日，总理迪芬贝克在该山口宣布横加公路通车。

timeline.en: Rogers Pass is designated a national historic site. Construction under the Trans-Canada Highway Act ends the same year.
timeline.zh: 罗杰斯山口被列为国家历史遗址。《横加公路法》下的建设亦于同年结束。

timeline.en: A statue of Terry Fox by Nathan Scott is installed beside the Mile 0 monument, at the end of the run he did not finish.
timeline.zh: 内森·斯科特创作的特里·福克斯雕像立于零英里碑旁——那是他未能跑完的终点。
